title: He asked for more.
paragraphs:
Not more fame.
Not more followers.
More of God.
But here’s what will shake you:

It didn’t start with power.
It started with surrender.

Fire from heaven.
Public victory.
Visible authority.
But they skip the hidden years…

The silent obedience…
The unnoticed service…
The moments where no one claps.
And that’s where we lose it.

You pray… but you check if someone noticed.
You serve… but it hurts when no one thanks you.
You obey… but only when it benefits your image.
That’s pride wearing a worship mask.
And this is where the story cuts deep.
He began by pouring water on someone else’s hands (2 Kings 3:11).

Before he ever touched power…
he embraced humility.
We want God to use us…
…but avoid the process that forms the vessel.
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” — James 4:6

That means the very thing blocking your breakthrough
might not be your circumstances…
Some scholars interpret Elisha’s request for a “double portion” (2 Kings 2:9) as the inheritance of a firstborn son—not selfish ambition, but a desire to carry forward Elijah’s spiritual legacy.
But even that kind of calling demands death.
And here’s the part no one posts about:
He walked through moments where nothing happened.
And that’s where many walk away.

Because hidden obedience feels like failure
when your heart is addicted to visibility.

God is not building your platform.
He’s building your character.
And if He gave you power without purity—
Because this is where everything shifts.
we don’t just struggle with pride.
“All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
We want to be our own god.
But God didn’t leave us there.
He stepped into our pride-filled world…
not as a king demanding applause—
“He humbled Himself by becoming obedient to the point of death—even death on a cross.” — Philippians 2:8
The One who deserved all glory…
The One who could command angels…
The One who had no sin…
Because your pride needed a Savior.

your need for recognition…
your hidden arrogance…
your subtle self-worship…
He opened a new way of living.
A life not driven by ego…
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.” — 2 Corinthians 5:17
“Why am I not being used more?”
“Am I willing to be hidden if it means becoming like Christ?”
“Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.” — Matthew 23:12
Elisha’s story isn’t about outperforming Elijah.
It’s about a man who said:
I just need God to move.”

The need to prove yourself.
The craving for validation.
The quiet pride you’ve been protecting.

Turn from self…
and turn to Christ.
“Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will lift you up.” — James 4:10
That’s where God does His deepest work.
Because when the vessel is ready…

From hidden obedience to undeniable power.
From pride to surrender.
From self to Savior.
